findings.title: Costs
findings.text: Slippage and commissions cost 0.069R per trade on average (+0.042R before costs, -0.027R after). Before costs the setups made money; costs erase it.

findings.title: Win rate vs what's needed
findings.text: Win rate 38.1% against about 39.1% needed to break even with the actual average winner (+1.61R) and loser (-1.03R). Median target was 2.0R; only 23.8% of trades ever reached +2R before exiting.

findings.title: False breakouts
findings.text: 34.8% of stopped trades were stopped within 2 bars of entry: the move reversed almost immediately. Not unusually high.

findings.title: Giving back winners
findings.text: 17.2% of losing trades were up at least +1R at some point before turning into a loss. Few losers were ever meaningfully profitable, so exit management isn't the main problem.

findings.title: Stop placement
findings.text: 16.3% of stopped trades went on to reach the original target later the same day; 40.5% of those never went more than 1.5R against the entry first, so a somewhat wider stop might have held. Wider stops mean smaller positions, so this is a trade-off to test, not a fix.

findings.title: Long vs short
findings.text: Best: short +0.166R over 427 trades (95% interval [-0.089, 0.409]). Worst: long -0.224R over 416 trades (interval [-0.36, -0.1]).

findings.title: Trading with or against the trend
findings.text: Best: no clear trend +0.031R over 58 trades (95% interval [-0.335, 0.458]). Worst: against trend -0.112R over 270 trades (interval [-0.26, 0.035]).

findings.title: Time of day
findings.text: Best: 10:00-11:30 morning +0.070R over 200 trades (95% interval [-0.14, 0.295]). Worst: 14:00-16:00 afternoon -0.091R over 194 trades (interval [-0.242, 0.082]).

findings.title: Choppy markets
findings.text: Best: trending / expanding -0.013R over 720 trades (95% interval [-0.12, 0.1]). Worst: choppy / consolidating -0.104R over 123 trades (interval [-0.335, 0.132]).

findings.title: Late / extended entries
findings.text: Best: extended (>1.5 ATR from 9 EMA) +0.015R over 167 trades (95% interval [-0.297, 0.361]). Worst: near 9 EMA (<=1.5 ATR) -0.037R over 676 trades (interval [-0.109, 0.037]).

findings.title: Volume confirmation
findings.text: Best: volume confirmed +0.031R over 120 trades (95% interval [-0.304, 0.317]). Worst: weak volume -0.036R over 723 trades (interval [-0.127, 0.065]).

findings.title: Volatility
findings.text: Best: high-vol +0.034R over 338 trades (95% interval [-0.156, 0.223]). Worst: normal-vol -0.068R over 505 trades (interval [-0.154, 0.024]).

findings.title: Checklist score
findings.text: Best: checklist >= 70 +0.010R over 235 trades (95% interval [-0.207, 0.208]). Worst: checklist < 50 -0.067R over 329 trades (interval [-0.207, 0.071]).

findings.title: Setups that clearly lose
findings.text: level_breakout (long) (-0.306R, 86 trades). These are switched to NO TRADE in live signals.

findings.title: Setups with positive evidence
findings.text: None. No setup or ticker slice has an out-of-sample 95% interval entirely above zero.

diagnostics.caveat: These slices describe past out-of-sample trades. Choosing filters from them and re-testing on the same trades would be curve-fitting; any idea here must be confirmed on later data.

search.note: Each fold tried 1 parameter combinations on its training window and kept the best. The more combinations tried, the more the training winner is a lucky draw - which is exactly why only the following, unseen test window is reported.
